title: A reduction scheme for general-order Ising-like Hamiltonians in quantum heuristic solvers
authors: Chengsi Mao, Pavel Mosharev, Yao Wang, Man-Hong Yung
abstract: The Ising model is ubiquitous in various optimization problems but notoriously difficult to solve due to combinatorial explosion. In view of this, Hamiltonian reduction is a useful preprocessing technique for reducing the effective problem size before applying heuristic solvers. However, existing reduction techniques mainly target second-order Ising models, whereas many pseudo-Boolean formulations naturally contain higher-order interactions. In this work, we generalize the concept of non-separable groups to arbitrary-order Ising-like models and develop a Hamiltonian reduction framework that iteratively detects and merges constrained spin groups into single variables. We benchmark the reduction on synthetic hypergraphs and higher-order network datasets, and evaluate its integration with downstream order-reduction and solver workflows. Our results establish a foundation for Hamiltonian reduction in higher-order Ising-like optimization problems.
summary: This paper introduces GeneralHare, a novel Hamiltonian reduction framework designed to handle general-order Ising-like Hamiltonians beyond the scope of existing second-order methods. By generalizing non-separability theory, it effectively reduces complex optimization problems defined on hypergraphs into smaller, equivalent forms. This advancement provides a crucial preprocessing step for applying quantum heuristic solvers to more realistic, higher-order physical models.
main_problem: The core problem is developing a Hamiltonian reduction framework for general-order Ising-like Hamiltonians, as existing techniques are limited to second-order interactions while real problems contain higher-order terms.
main_result: The proposed GeneralHare scheme successfully generalizes non-separability theory to arbitrary orders, achieving superior reduction ratios and performance compared to prior methods like FastHare on synthetic and public hypergraph datasets.
method: The authors generalize the concept of 'non-separable groups' to create a generalized non-separable group (gNG) and develop the GeneralHare framework to iteratively detect and merge these constrained spin groups into single variables, thereby reducing the effective problem size.
model_or_system: The model is the general-order Ising-like Hamiltonian defined on hypergraphs, $H( oldsymbol{\sigma}) = \sum J_I \prod_{i \in I} \sigma_i$, which are benchmarked using synthetic (ER/SF) and public network datasets.
key_observables: Reduction ratio ($r$), solution energy $H(\sigma)$, computational runtime, and final variable count overhead after reduction.
important_parameters: The order of the Hamiltonian ($M$), the structure of the hypergraph (e.g., ER-like vs. SF-like), and the candidate-size cutoff parameter ($\xi$).
main_assumptions: Existing methods are limited to second-order models, and the reconstruction process relies on tracking explicit node maps to ensure ground state correspondence.
figures_summary: Figures compare reduction ratios and performance (Energy/Runtime) of GeneralHare against FastHare and Order Reduction techniques across various hypergraph types; Figure 1 illustrates the general structure of the higher-order Hamiltonian.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the limitations of current methods, proposes the generalized non-separable group concept, details the GeneralHare framework for reduction, benchmarks this framework on synthetic and public datasets, and finally evaluates its integration into downstream quantum heuristic solvers (like bSB).
why_interesting: While focused on classical optimization, the underlying mathematical structure—analyzing complex interactions in high-dimensional spin systems—is highly relevant to understanding energy landscapes in quantum many-body physics, particularly those involving higher-order couplings.
